scenes.title: Pudding Lane
scenes.purpose: Place the viewer at the exact origin in time and place: one bakery, just after midnight.
scenes.visual: A torn map sheet slides onto kraft paper; a taped banner names the lane; a paper flame is pinned to one spot and flickers beside a tiny bakery cut-out.

transition_out.continuity: the next paper sheet is pushed over the last: time moves on

scenes.narration: A little after midnight on Sunday the second of September, sixteen sixty-six, a fire broke out in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane.

layout.landscape: map sheet left-centre, banner top-right, flame pinned low-centre

scenes.title: Sunday to Wednesday
scenes.purpose: Show duration and how it ended: four days, ended when the wind dropped and firebreaks held.
scenes.visual: Four day tickets are stamped down one by one as a torn burn-shape spreads across a schematic city and turns to charcoal when the wind note is taped on.

transition_out.continuity: a torn-edge wipe: the sheet is ripped away to reveal what was lost

scenes.narration: It burned until Wednesday. Only when the wind dropped and firebreaks took hold was the fire finally over.

layout.landscape: day tickets in a row across the top, burn shape lower-left spreading right

scenes.title: The loss
scenes.purpose: State the scale of the loss with the sources' own ranges.
scenes.visual: A huge counter on a torn vermilion sheet rolls to 13,200 while a row of paper houses chars one by one, then a row of churches and a dome fall to charcoal and are stamped RUIN.

transition_out.continuity: calm: the loud sheet fades from one object, not a scene wipe

scenes.narration: By then, an estimated thirteen thousand houses, about eighty-seven parish churches, and Saint Paul's Cathedral had been destroyed.

layout.landscape: counter sheet left, house row beneath, church row and dome right

scenes.title: How many died?
scenes.purpose: Be honest that the human cost is uncertain, and give that uncertainty room.
scenes.visual: Almost empty kraft: one typed line, a single paper '6' in a circle, and a lightly ghosted question mark that grows behind it.

transition_out.continuity: the paper '6' circle carries over and becomes the dome: the calm circle turns into the rebuilt city

scenes.narration: The death toll is still debated. The traditional figure is just six, but some historians think it was far higher.

layout.landscape: line upper-left third, circle sticker right of centre, lots of paper

scenes.title: Brick and stone
scenes.purpose: Show what changed: a different city, built in brick and stone, with the Monument as memory.
scenes.visual: The circle sticker becomes the dome of St Paul's; bricks stack into a skyline replacing timber houses, WOOD is struck out, and a paper column grows to a 202 ft tape-measure label. It ends smaller than it began.
scenes.narration: London was rebuilt in brick and stone, not wood. Christopher Wren rebuilt Saint Paul's, and the Monument, two hundred and two feet tall, still marks the fire.

layout.landscape: skyline across the lower half, dome left, Monument column right, title small centre
